images.filename: M41A3 Walker Bulldog at the 823 Artillery Battle Memorial Park, Taichung, Taiwan. 07-03-2026 (55256041835).jpg
images.caption:
Taiwan received around 700 M41s as military aid from the United States. The last M41A3s were not retired until 2022, although the upgraded M41D remains in service as of 2026.
823 Artillery Battle Memorial Park, Taichung, Taiwan.

7th March 2026
images.alt:

images.artist: Alan Wilson from Peterborough, Cambs, UK

images.filename: M24A1 Chaffee at the 823 Artillery Battle Memorial Park, Taichung, Taiwan. 07-03-2026 (55254718262).jpg
images.caption:
Designed to replace the M5 Stuart, some 4,731 Chaffee’s were produced between April 1944 and August 1945. Taiwan received 233 Chaffee’s in 1954 under the Sino-US Mutual Defence Treaty and then 56 more in 1966.
This is one of several which were upgraded to M24A1 standard, with a Detroit 6V-53T diesel engine and other minor modifications.
823 Artillery Battle Memorial Park, Taichung, Taiwan.

7th March 2026
images.alt:

images.filename: M108 Self-Propelled Gun at the 823 Artillery Battle Memorial Park, Taichung, Taiwan. 07-03-2026 (55255877419).jpg
images.caption:
The M108 was an American, Cold-War era, self-propelled gun, which saw US service between 1962 and 1975. Produced by Cadillac, it had a crew of five and was armed with the M103 105mm howitzer. Taiwan operated one-hundred M108s, forty-five of which were later modernised to T69 standard with an M59 155mm gun. This preserved example is an un-modified M108.
823 Artillery Battle Memorial Park, Taichung, Taiwan.

7th March 2026
